national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today spoke with Captain Smit Machchhar over the phone, praising his bravery and presence of mind in foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight. The Prime Minister said, Indians are not those who take lives, but those who are willing to risk their own lives to save others. He lauded Captain Machchhar for taking a split-second decision that helped save the lives of hundreds of passengers. On Wednesday, Captain Machchhar got seriously injured after being stabbed by his co-pilot in the cockpit of Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children. The pilot is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. Speaking to the Prime Minister from his hospital bed, Captain Machchhar said his 17 years of flying experience, including 11 years as a captain, helped him understand the gravity of the situation and act immediately. He told the Prime Minister that he is away from the country but not from its culture. Prime Minister Modi said, special prayers were being offered across India for the pilot’s speedy recovery and thanked the governments of Saudi Arabia and the UAE for ensuring his treatment. The Prime Minister also said Captain Machchhar had enhanced the prestige of the Indian piloting community. Referring to Gandhi Jayanti being observed today, Mr Modi said the pilot had shown the world the true meaning of Ahimsa (non-violence). Captain Machchhar, who hails from Gujarat, expressed gratitude to the Prime Minister for the call and said he was receiving the best possible treatment. Mr Modi also spoke to him briefly in Gujarati.

national_raw_news.title: Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief ...
national_raw_news.content: Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief over tragic deaths - The Sangai Express - Largest Circulated NewsPaper in Manipur Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief over tragic deaths 02-Oct-2026 | IMPHAL, Oct 2 (PIB) The Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Imphal, have expressed profound grief over the tragic demise of Dr Engam Pame, Additional Director General, PIB & CBC Regional Office, Imphal; Nampibou Marinmai, Director (News), DDK and All India Radio (AIR), Aizawl, and H Lianvela, Multi-Tasking Staff member, CBC, Aizawl, who lost their lives in a tragic road accident near Sateek in Mizoram on Thursday. Dr Engam Pame was a senior Indian Information Service (IIS) officer serving as Additional Director General, PIB & CBC Regional Office, Imphal. He joined the PIB/CBC Regional Office, Imphal, on July 29, 2022, as Regional Director. During his distinguished career, he had also served as Director, Directorate of Field Publicity, Shillong, and had been associated with the Regional News Unit of Doordarshan Kendra, Imphal. He was the Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC), Manipur Chapter, it said. Born on November 30, 1967, Dr Pame made significant contributions to public communication and information dissemination, it added. During his tenure at PIB and CBC, Imphal, he played an important role in strengthening coordination between the Government and the media fraternity and in facilitating the dissemination of information on government Golicies, programmes and initiatives, it said. The statement continued that Nampibou Marinmai was also an IIS officer and was serving as Director (News), DDK and AIR, Aizawl. He was Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC) and had earlier served as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. During his tenure with the Ministry of Defence, he was associated with defence-related public relations, media reporting and communication. Through his long association with news and public broadcasting, the PIB said that Marinmai made valuable contributions to public communication and information dissemination. Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw expressed deep sorrow over the demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai and H Lianvela and conveyed his heartfelt condolences to their bereaved families, friends and colleagues. Several senior officials of the Ministry and its attached organisations also expressed deep sorrow over the tragic loss and conveyed their heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. They expressed solidarity with the families, friends and colleagues of the departed during this hour of immense grief. The Ministry of Defence also mourned the demise of Nampibou Marinmai, recalling his services as Public Relations Officer (Defence) and his long-standing association with defence reporting. Officials and staff of PIB, CBC and Akashvani, Imphal, observed a two-minute silence in memory of the departed souls and expressed their deepest condolences to the bereaved families. They also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured driver and extended their support and solidarity to those affected by the tragedy....
